key_insight: A PPO-based controller can coordinate battery, hydrogen, diesel, and grid exchange in a community microgrid to keep supply highly reliable while maximizing annual operating revenue.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how reinforcement learning can improve real-time energy management for hydrogen-enabled microgrids that must balance renewable variability, storage coupling, and outage resilience.
method: Formulated microgrid dispatch as an 11-state Markov decision process with three continuous actions for battery, diesel, and hydrogen control.
Used proximal policy optimization (PPO) to learn operating policies from hourly community-scale data.
Evaluated grid-connected operation with PV, wind, battery, electrolyzer, hydrogen storage, fuel cell, diesel backup, and grid exchange inferred from power balance.
evidence_signal: Validated on 8,760 hourly observations for a 1,000-household community in Rockhampton, Australia, achieving A$195,690.67 revenue, 91.2% renewable fraction, 99.77% load satisfaction, and 0.085 kg CO2/kWh under the stated boundary.
watch_item: Performance is sensitive to renewable variability, training stability, and the selected carbon-accounting/evaluation boundary, so real-world deployment needs careful validation.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy Management for Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids Under Uncertainty
